body:
This happens because we only rewrite URLs to `/index.html` if they don't contains an file extension.
I wouldn't rewrite other URLs to `/index.html`, because that would make them look like 200 responses, but we could add an aio-themed [404.html page][1].

[1]: https://firebase.google.com/docs/hosting/url-redirects-rewrites#section-404
Hm...although it would not be straightforward to keep this consistent with `/index.html` (in looks and behavior) 😕

issue.title: fix(aio): show aio-themed 404 page for unknown resources

body:
> because that would make them look like 200 responses, 

I don't think this is true, since we create "soft-404s" for non-existent pages.

So redirecting all 404 pages to `index.html` would seem a reasonable approach and would keep the project simpler, rather than having to generate a static 404 page at build time.

I don't think it is a good idea to have soft 404s for resources. Soft 404s are still technically 200s and resources could be requested not as top-level documents (i.e. navigation requests) but as....resources (e.g. images).
Images in the docs are checked by dgeni so we shouldn't have any 404s from doc pages.
Not sure what the usecase is, but I am pretty sure it is not about us referencing nob-existent resources ('cause we would never do that :grin:)
I thought it was 3rd party websites linking to outdated resources
